issues.title: Spike: does Boris forward the verified caller identity to MCP tools?
issues.body:
## Why
The wallet can only apply personal caps if it knows WHO is buying. This is the biggest technical risk.

## Questions
- Which identity information reaches a downstream MCP tool (header, claim, DID)?
- Can tool gating differ per caller (parent / teen / child)?
- Fallback if not: separate Boris access points per role, or a signed member token passed as tool argument.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Answer documented in `doc/research/boris_identity_spike.md` with evidence (screenshot/log)
- [ ] Chosen approach agreed by the team

issues.title: Epic E7: Discount honesty check (from ticket #25)
issues.body:
## Goal
Before the family spends money on a "reduced" product, the agent checks whether the discount is real: genuine deal, inflated "was" price, or real discount but cheaper elsewhere. Idea from ticket #25 (Pukhraj97); the design was reviewed and corrected in `doc/design/discount_check.md`.

## Done when
- [ ] The corrected design and diagram exist and name what was wrong in the ticket's formula
- [ ] `check_discount` is a deterministic, integer-only function with tests DC-01…DC-19 at 100%
- [ ] The agent calls it before ordering a reduced product and reports the verdict

Not in scope (from the ticket): Node/TypeScript service, web app, 90-day history, category-graph substitutes — idealo MCP offers 30 days of history and no category graph.

Stories are the sub-issues of this epic; tasks are the checkboxes inside each story.

issues.title: Review ticket #25 and write the corrected discount-check design
issues.parent: Epic E7: Discount honesty check (from ticket #25)
issues.body:
## Why
The ticket's scorer `claimed_discount >= (list_price - 30_day_low) / list_price` reduces to `sale <= 30_day_low`; it never tests whether the "was" price is inflated.

## Tasks
- [ ] Assessment table: sound / wrong / unverified (`doc/design/discount_check.md`)
- [ ] Corrected integer algorithm: reference = lowest price in the 30 days before the reduction; tolerance 100 basis points; minimum 7 history points
- [ ] Decision flow diagram `doc/diagrams/discount_check.mmd`
- [ ] Test table DC-01…DC-19 with exact cent values

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every verdict (INVALID_INPUT, NO_DISCOUNT_CLAIMED, INSUFFICIENT_HISTORY, INFLATED, NOT_BEST_PRICE, GENUINE) has a rule and a reason text
- [ ] Open questions for the owner are listed (source of `sale_days`, what idealo's price history really contains)

issues.title: Implement check_discount: pure function, MCP tool and tests DC-01…DC-19
issues.parent: Epic E7: Discount honesty check (from ticket #25)
issues.body:
## Why
A rule-based verdict can be proven with test cases; an LLM opinion cannot.

## Tasks
- [ ] `src/family_shopper/discount_check.py` (integer cents and basis points, no I/O)
- [ ] Tool `check_discount` on the idealo mock server (`src/family_shopper/idealo_mock/server.py`)
- [ ] `tests/test_discount_check.py`: one test per row DC-01…DC-19
- [ ] Fixtures: one inflated product (headphones, was 449 €, 30-day low 310 €) and one genuine one

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `uv run pytest -q tests/test_discount_check.py tests/test_idealo_mock.py` passes 100%
- [ ] Passes in GitHub Actions on the pull request

## Acceptance criteria

issues.title: Parent can reject an approval request

## Why
Owner decision 2026-11-27: a parent can say no. Until now a request could only stay open or be approved.

- [ ] Wallet: parent only, one write transaction, status `rejected`, no order, no spend
- [ ] `list_requests` accepts `rejected`
- [ ] Tests: role refusal, reject twice, approve after reject, concurrent approve and reject

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `uv run pytest -q` green in GitHub Actions

issues.title: An inflated discount blocks the order
issues.parent: Epic E7: Discount honesty check (from ticket #25)
issues.body:
## Why
Owner decision 2026-11-27: verdict INFLATED blocks the order (before: warn only).

## Tasks
- [ ] Purchase path of the web UI server: `check_discount` before the wallet call when a "was" price is claimed; INFLATED → no wallet call
- [ ] System prompt: INFLATED → do not order
- [ ] Eval scenario S-13 and the updated S-11

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Headphones "was 449 €" → blocked, zero orders in the wallet
- [ ] A genuine discount still orders

Limit: the wallet has no price history and cannot verify a discount itself; the block lives in the purchase path and in the agent.

issues.title: Budget rule: up to the budget the wallet decides, above it a parent steps in (teen and child)
issues.body:
## Why
Owner decisions 2026-11-27 evening, replacing "every child order needs a parent": up to the member's own budget the trust layer decides; above it the order is refused and a parent steps in. A parent-approved order counts against the member's budget and the family budget.

## Tasks
- [x] Wallet: child and teen `place_order` within the personal and family budget; above it `PERSONAL_CAP_EXCEEDED` with "A parent can step in"
- [x] Wallet: `request_approval` for child and teen; `approve_request` checks the family cap only; remaining never negative
- [x] Server: 409 `canAskParent`; route `POST /api/family/request-approval`; chat tool `request_parent_approval`
- [x] Offers: "Within your budget" / "Above your budget — a parent can step in"
- [x] Tests `tests/test_child_budget_rule.py`; evals S-15, S-16, S-17; harness invariant counts approved spend
- [ ] Limit on open requests per member (reviewer remark: unlimited today)

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] No order above a member's budget without a parent's approval (30-thread race tests, adversarial driver)
- [x] Child part merged by PR #69 after independent review
- [ ] Teen part merged (PR #70, review pending)

issues.title: Board follows pull requests automatically (In progress on open, Test on merge)
issues.parent: Epic E6: Dev environment and orchestration
issues.body:
## Why
The board was synced by hand and fell three rounds behind the code (2026-11-27). Owner decision: automate board updates.

## Rule
Stories are named in the pull request title, e.g. `feat: … (#7, #8)`. PR opened → those stories move to In progress; PR merged → to Test with a comment. Epics and pull request numbers are ignored. Demo-ready and checkbox ticks stay manual.

## Tasks
- [ ] `scripts/board_sync.py` with unit tests (`tests/test_board_sync.py`)
- [ ] `.github/workflows/board-sync.yml` (`pull_request_target`, never checks out the PR head, untrusted title only through env)
- [ ] Runbook `doc/runbooks/board_automation.md`
- [ ] **Owner:** create a classic token with only the `project` scope and store it as the repository secret `PROJECT_TOKEN`
- [ ] First real workflow run seen moving a card

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Without the secret the workflow skips and does not fail
- [ ] With the secret: a PR naming a story moves its card on open and on merge
